description: Claude Code has FINISHED its turn: the completed-turn marker reads '✛ Churned for 1m 13s · done 10:28 PM' (a wall-clock completion stamp, not 'esc to interrupt'), and the user has typed an unsent draft into the input box. The pane is idle at the prompt. The regression this guards: this exact screen was served to the phone as activity 'running' for 36 minutes, showing a green Running badge on a finished agent and sorting it as recently active. The cause was not the prompt — the model reads this screen correctly — but the no-LLM fallback in classify(), which defaulted a failed parse to 'running' whenever the tail was not a bare shell prompt (i.e. always, on an agent TUI). This sample pins the screen itself so a future prompt edit cannot start reading a finished turn, or an unsent draft, as live work.
capture:
It doesn't, much — but it's a symptom of the same underlying thing. That Chrome process has been alive for 7 days because it was launched as a one-shot auth handoff and then
  just… never got cleaned up. Same story as the 21 claude processes, the 5-day-old codex, and the 17 npm exec @vanta workers. Your machine is carrying a week of detritus from
  finished sessions.

  Note the load average moved since my earlier read: 4.15 / 4.64 / 3.79 in your screenshot, down from 11.04. So the spike I saw has passed, and CPU is 92.8% idle. If YouTube is
  still chunking right now, the cause is more likely thermal (you were at 78°C package temp with two cores capped at 1.6 GHz) than contention.

  Two things I'd still do, and I want your call on the second:

  1. Kill PID 86841's stale auth tab — safe, it's a dead code. Though note it's the Chrome main process, so closing it takes your whole Chrome session with it. Probably better to
     just let it be, or restart Chrome when convenient.
  2. Reap the day-plus-old agent processes. Still ~15 GB and a lot of scheduler churn.

  My earlier offer stands and you didn't get a chance to answer it: want me to list the claude/codex/vanta processes older than 24 hours with their working directories, so you
  can see which are dead sessions before anything gets terminated? I won't touch falcon-sensor or anything recent.
